nodes.label: Central question: break the chain or pass it on?
nodes.rationale: When chance hands you power, do you break the chain you inherited, or pass it on? The book never answers.

nodes.label: Luck (the chance that hands him power)
Pillar 1: Family and descent
nodes.rationale: Family is both the wound and the cure; what is offered as a choice can be refused.

nodes.label: Pillar 2: Luck
nodes.rationale: Nobody chooses where they start; what a person does with their luck is the only part that is theirs.

nodes.label: Pillar 3: Freedom and its price
nodes.rationale: Freedom can be bought, but not the name or the honour; everyone wants to be the master.

nodes.label: Pillar 4: Violence
nodes.rationale: Force makes things of everyone it touches, whoever bears it and whoever wields it.

nodes.label: Carmen is not the villain spoiling the boys
nodes.rationale: She offers them the easier world he fought to reach.

nodes.label: The book as a descendant's search
nodes.rationale: Benedito searches for his mother; his sons never know him; the author searches for an ancestor whose name is lost.

nodes.label: Many kinds of freedom: law, money, the inner kind
nodes.rationale: He wins the first two and never the third.

nodes.label: Free from, and free to: the father and the sons
Nobody is free from what they carry
Freedom bought and sold; money and paper
Everyone wants to be the master
nodes.rationale: The whole society shows it, the white characters first; never mainly the formerly enslaved.

nodes.label: No one is guilt-free, and no one is condemned
Dona Pires
nodes.rationale: Rules her salon by deciding who belongs.
